newsitem.title: USA: Aradigm says inhaled insulin study positive.
newsitem.headline: Aradigm says inhaled insulin study positive.

text.p: Aradigm Corp said Monday that results of a clinical study show diabetics may be able to control meal-time glucose levels by inhaling insulin.
The company said inadequate control of meal-time glucose levels is known to cause serious long-term medical problems for diabetics.
The company said many patients fail to take their meal-time insulin because it must be delivered by subcutaneous injection.

The company said a non-invasive inhaled insulin may allow more patients to better control their glucose levels and therefore delay or avoid many of the long-term complications associated with diabetes.

The company said the study results were presented by Dr. Igor Gonda, Aradigm's vice president of research and development, at the Western Regional Meeting of the American Association of Pharmaceutical Scientists held on April 24-25 in South San Francisco, California.
